verses.english: Linked Discourses 4.6
1. Lifespan
A Serpent
So I have heard.

verses.pali: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe.
verses.english: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha, in the Bamboo Grove, the squirrels’ feeding ground.

verses.pali: Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā rattandhakāratimisāyaṁ abbhokāse nisinno hoti, devo ca ekamekaṁ phusāyati.
verses.english: Now at that time the Buddha was meditating in the open during the dark of night, while a gentle rain drizzled down.

verses.pali: Atha kho māro pāpimā bhagavato bhayaṁ chambhitattaṁ lomahaṁsaṁ uppādetukāmo mahantaṁ sapparājavaṇṇaṁ abhinimminitvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami.
verses.english: Then Māra the Wicked, wanting to make the Buddha feel fear, terror, and goosebumps, manifested in the form of a huge serpent king and approached him.
Its body was like a huge canoe carved from a single tree.
Its hood was like a large brewer’s sieve.
Its eyes were like big bronze cups from Kosala.

verses.pali: Seyyathāpi nāma deve gaḷagaḷāyante vijjullatā niccharanti;
verses.english: Its tongue flickered from its mouth like lightning flashes in a thunderstorm.

verses.pali: Seyyathāpi nāma kammāragaggariyā dhamamānāya saddo hoti;
verses.english: The sound of its breathing was like the puffing of a blacksmith’s bellows.

verses.pali: Atha kho bhagavā “māro ayaṁ pāpimā” iti viditvā māraṁ pāpimantaṁ gāthāhi ajjhabhāsi:
verses.english: Then the Buddha, knowing that this was Māra the Wicked, replied to him in verse:
“A self-controlled sage frequents
empty buildings for lodging.
It’s appropriate for that sort
to live there after relinquishing.
Though there are lots of creepy crawlies,
and lots of flies and snakes,
they wouldn’t stir a hair
of a great sage in that empty hut.
Though the firmament may split <j>and the earth may quake,
and all creatures be stricken with fear;
and even if an arrow’s aimed at their breast,
the Buddhas take no shelter in attachments.”

verses.pali: Atha kho māro pāpimā “jānāti maṁ bhagavā, jānāti maṁ sugato”ti dukkhī dummano tatthevantaradhāyīti.
verses.english: Then Māra the Wicked, thinking, “The Buddha knows me! The Holy One knows me!” miserable and sad, vanished right there.
